name: Heresies of the Early Church

objectives.text: Identify a heresy as a false teaching about God that disagrees with what the Bible says
State that Jesus is both true God and true man, the truth that many early false teachers denied
Describe how early Christians tested a teaching by comparing it with the words of Scripture and the apostles
Retell how the apostles warned that false teachers would arise and how church leaders were charged to guard believers from them
Summarize the Gnostic teaching that the material world and the body are evil and that secret knowledge saves
Explain why the Arian claim that the Son was created contradicts what Scripture teaches about the Word who made all things
Explain the Docetic claim that Jesus only seemed to be human and show how the apostles answered it from his bodily life and resurrection
Compare a heresy to a counterfeit by identifying what it borrows from true teaching and what it changes
Describe Marcion's rejection of the Old Testament and its God and explain how Scripture presents one God and one story across both testaments
Distinguish modalism (Sabellianism) from the doctrine of the Trinity using passages where Father, Son, and Spirit act distinctly
Explain the Ebionite and adoptionist claims that Jesus was a mere man later made Son of God and identify texts that affirm his eternal deity
Analyze how Marcion's shortened canon pressed the early church to recognize which books belonged in Scripture
Compare Pelagius's teaching that people can obey God without inward grace with what Scripture says about sin inherited from Adam
Connect an ancient heresy to the teaching of a modern religious group, such as Arianism and the Jehovah's Witnesses' denial of Christ's deity
Analyze how Montanism's claims of new prophecy challenged the sufficiency of the apostolic Scriptures
Explain the Donatist claim that a sacrament's validity depends on the holiness of the minister and the church's answer to it
Analyze a passage from Irenaeus's Against Heresies to identify how he answered Gnostic teaching by appeal to Scripture and the apostolic rule of faith
Classify the Christological heresies of the early centuries, including Docetism, Ebionism, Arianism, Apollinarianism, Nestorianism, and Eutychianism, by the truth about Christ's person each denies
Explain why the early church held that the Redeemer must be both fully God and fully man to save, as the Reformed confessions also teach
Evaluate how the church's response to heresy led it to sharpen doctrinal language such as the term homoousios
Defend the Reformed doctrine of human inability against Pelagian and semi-Pelagian claims using Scripture and the confessions
Evaluate the criteria the early church used to distinguish orthodoxy from heresy, including Scripture, the apostolic rule of faith, and the consensus of the churches
Write an essay that traces a modern teaching to an ancient heresy and answers it from Scripture and the Reformed confessions

changes: Removed every reference to the Nicene Creed. Doctrines it had anchored are now cited to library documents: Westminster Shorter Catechism Q6 and Q21, Westminster Confession of Faith 2.3, and Belgic Confession Articles 9 and 10. Dropped filler and devotional objectives (careful what we listen to, the Bible helps us spot lies, apply the need to know the real Jesus). Reworded and kept the real competencies: defining heresy, Gnosticism, Arianism, the counterfeit comparison, Marcionism, Pelagianism, modern parallels, Docetism, the Christological taxonomy, the church's response, and the defense against Pelagius. Recast the orthodoxy synthesis as an evaluation of the early church's criteria. Added objectives on testing teaching by Scripture, apostolic warnings, modalism, Ebionism and adoptionism, Marcion and the canon, Montanism, Donatism, Irenaeus as a source, why the Redeemer must be God and man, and a capstone essay. Material on the councils and creeds themselves is left to the sibling sub-topic.
